doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

title: The frustration of composing
summary: Davis says composition is frustrating, carried in the head, and requires patience with oneself.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: If you’re in the midst of arranging a piece do you carry it around with you in your head even when you’re not working on it?

Yeah a hundred percent, yeah. And sometimes to the point of I want it to leave my head and I can’t get it out of my head. And then of course there’s the — you’re committed to it and you’ve done it all and it’s still in your head and you realize oh I wish I had done something different. That’s often part of the equation. So I find it to be a pretty frustrating process to be honest with you Monk, composition in general. And you hear these great songwriters talk about it from Billy Joel to Sting to Carla Bley, you know all range of styles. And a lot of them say the same thing you know and you’re writing and writing and then it’s just terrible so you throw it away and you start again and you just wasted the whole day. But that’s part of the process I think and all these great composers always kind of allude to that so I think you have to give yourself, you have to be kind to yourself © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

I think when you’re writing ‘cause it’s not just going to flow out of you even if you’re really good at it. It’s trial and error. Some things are going to work, some things aren’t and you’re going to want to change stuff. So you’ve got to give yourself some patience.
